utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom, and also in the surrounding technicals and interpreters' booths. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think before we continue the cross-examination of the witness, Mr. Besic, I'd like to make a few remarks. First, I'd refer to the rather tumultuous end of the Court session of yesterday. If Counsel was acting diligently and skillfully, we would have avoided the confusion that came up yesterday in respect of whether the videotape to be played was the same as the videotape played on Monday. I checked the exhibits list according to Article 65 ter, and it becomes rather clear from that tape, apart from that the tapes have different numbers, that the origin seem to be at least not the same. That's my first observation. The second one is, has the Prosecution been able to find out exactly -- I don't want an answer now because we're in open session -- about Witness Q?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we'll hear that on short notice. And did you write the answer down or will you give it in writing or will you tell it orally to the Court? Not at this moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We did not write it, but much of what we were going to say but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We did not write it. I did not realise that we had been asked to write it. We could do so later. Most of what I would say has been recorded in motions filed previously, so I would refer the Court to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll be in private session somewhere, so I'll ask you to explain to the Court. I assume that the information about the expert witnesses will come at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We will seek to clarify the status of each one and be more precise in the use of "expert." We would propose that we refer to experts in respect to Rule 94 bis as experts pursuant to Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we'll get a final answer to you by when, by tomorrow or?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tomorrow we're not sitting. We hope by Monday or Tuesday next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you. Tomorrow we're not sitting, the change of the Court schedule. Yes, if there's nothing else as preliminary matter -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, good morning to everybody here, and especially good morning to the Chamber. I have noted the remark of the Chamber, and I need to say the following,

utterances.speaker: MR. PRESIDENT
utterances.text: To begin with, this Defence asked to withdraw immediately this tape so as not to waste any time. But we were denied this by your Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My observation was not the start of a debate. It was an observation of the Chamber which is not in need for further debate at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will take note of that. But the sentence I wanted to say I've already done so, so I will sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think we are at the point where the cross-examination of Mr. Besic could be continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was about to ask a question. The second thing. Shall I say it, or shall I sit down?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's a question, I just wanted to make clear to you that the observation of the Chamber as such didn't need any debate. But of course if there's any question you'd like to put to the Court in respect of the continuation of the cross-examination, you are fully entitled to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is a question, not a debate. We have not received -- we have not received the other day, that is, this week, one exhibit or two exhibits which the Registry has which concern that tape, and the numbers are 2279 and 79A. And that is what causes the confusion. What I said the other day was that I believed it was this, I mean since we did not receive them, this produced the confusion. And since we do not have these exhibits, I don't know, we have not received the copies of these exhibits. And I do not know who I have to address myself to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me just first ask, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yesterday Mr. Stamp told us that 2279 was disclosed to you one year ago. On the other hand, it is usual that especially if there are any redacted versions and I understand that last Monday we started playing the redacted version of 2279, they are usually provided to the Defence. Has this been done, Mr. Stamp, or has it not been done?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It has been done. They were served with the original uncut some time ago, and the redacted version some time this year, some time recently. I am endeavouring to find the date of the service of the two tapes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, let's try to find out. The only thing that I noticed is that at least you make no observation as to the tape not being known to you when it was played to the witness, Besic. And I remember quite clearly that we discussed there were two versions, one version the redacted one, the shorter one with which we started. And then I think Mr. Stamp explained to us that he needed pieces of the video, of the original video as well, and that therefore he changed halfway to the long version of the video. And I'm not quite sure whether the redacted was 2279A, and the long version 2279. But perhaps, Madam Registrar, you could help us out, or Mr. Stamp. You are tendering them, at least one of them. Could you tell us which was the A version, was that the short version or the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The A version was the uncut original version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you started with 2279, and then later on you played 2279A, which is the long version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At that moment I didn't hear from the Defence, but that's no reason not to come back to it. I didn't hear from the Defence that they were not given this video, and -- but if you say we never received it, then the question is what to do at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. We are not saying that. We are not saying that. Simply the problem that we have, Mr. President, is that until we -- unless we receive in the courtroom such and such exhibit with a number, we are unable to check it with what we have. That is, whether this tape is exactly the same as what we have as a document. And that is a problem. For instance, when we have two documents in writing, we can compare them. But when we have two tapes which are relatively long, we cannot check it except by memory, and this is a rather -- it is more difficult an exercise. So except unless we see it in parallel, it is difficult to answer what is -- what I wanted to propose and what I wanted to do yesterday but was interrupted, that we be given on the video only what we were given by the Prosecution, and that will resolve every problem. That is what I wanted to propose yesterday but was not allowed to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I see that in the letter of the 27th of February, and I should check whether this is true for the earlier letters as well, I see it is also on the 25th of February, that it was indicated to you that the Prosecution would use Exhibit 2279. So may I assume that the Defence was prepared for the use of 2279?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, yes, Defence is prepared and was prepared. That is not the problem. The thing that we have to be sure of that tape which we received a year or more ago corresponds to what we received yesterday, what we heard yesterday, what we saw yesterday. And that resolves the debate. And that is what the Prosecution could be doing, that is, the Prosecution gives to the technical booth the tape that was used, be it the long one if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, do I understand you well that you want to be sure now that there's no more confusion about the tapes? That means two tapes have been given to the Registry, 2279 and 2279A. Did you -- it's not in my recollection -- did you then receive copies of the Registry at this very moment not, so you'd like to check. I think we're in a position that finally the Prosecution wants to tender the original long tape being the short one only excerpts of and the short one, that's 2279, only excerpts of the long one, the long one which is 227A. And it's a bit confusing, Mr. Stamp, because 2279A in the courtroom is 2279 on the Article 65 ter exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's also rather confusing. At least as soon as we establish that. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is it your purpose that you want to be sure that 2279A in Court is the same as 2279 on the Article 65 ter exhibit list?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the one hand -- on the one hand, Mr. President. But we are not talking here about the debate as you say. On the other hand, one of the tapes that we received has the number 2278, I repeat, 2278. And it seems that at this stage, the Prosecution has not produced the number 2278, even though we do not quite know the chronology of these exhibits. We have 2278 as an item of evidence, and we do not know whether this is related to the shelling of Markale. I'm checking this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2278 is on the exhibit list, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. And it is 2278, videotape, the shooting of Sarajevo market Markale 5th of February, 1994. So I expect to be on that tape some relevant information about the Markale market incident. Now, if you want to check whether these tapes I just mentioned are identical, I think this could be done outside the courtroom. But if you -- if there's a good reason, if you tell us that they are good reasons to believe they are not the same, we are not going to go through every video which is presented and compare it with the videos that have been presented one year before to the Defence. That would be impossible. But if there are good reasons to believe that the 2279A in Court would not be exactly the same as the Prosecution tells us as 2279 on the Article 65 ter exhibit list, of course then we should check it. There may be no question about that. But if we come to 2278, I think that that's a -- another video, and of course you can...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. We would have done that had the Prosecution immediately gave us the copy of 2279 and 2279A. This was not the case. But I am saying in principle to see that the tapes were identical. But what I wanted to do yesterday was to stop the debate and to give immediately simply the exhibits which the Registry has. What I have now and what I propose we do now is that those same tapes which the Registrar has so that we give them back to the booth. I believe that would be the best solution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I assume that you'd like to show part of any these videos to the witness. Which video you'd like to use? Is this 2278, of which we have not seen a single part?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll take the long one, and it should have, if I understood it well, letter A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's 2279A. You want to show parts of that video to the witness. Then, Madam Registrar, could the booth be provided with 2279A, which is the full-length version of what's on the exhibit list, 2279. And then -- unless there's any other reason, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very sorry, Mr. President, about this technical problem. But there is no doubt that all this would not have happened had we received in time and in place a copy of 2279 and 2279A which we could expect from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I also understand you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you're not going to use 2278, or what would I expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it always depends on the answers supplied by the witness. And over those, I'm not a master, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait and see what happens with 2278. It has been returned to you? Yes. Mr. Usher, could you then please bring Mr. Besic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Besic, good morning. Our apologies again that you had to wait for such -- please be seated. May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you gave last Monday. The cross-examination by Defence counsel will continue. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you'll start with this video or not? Would you please indicate to me the moment when you intend to play the video, because I'd like to explain to the witness the situation is a bit different from where we ended yesterday. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I will indicate it when we can have a look at the video, but not at the moment. At the moment, I would like -- I'm not getting any interpretation in my headphones, but perhaps it is normal. Oh, yes, I am. I'm sorry. I apologise. I would like to come back to some purely technical questions, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [interpretation] Witness, does the name Mr. Michel Guthier say something to you, for the transcript, Gauthier?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, do you know about results that came out of a mission of experts, UNPROFOR experts, resulting from the analysis that this expert mission carried out immediately following the incident of the 5th of February in Markale?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you say that you don't know anything about the results that came out of the analysis and the examination of these experts, and this was never communicated to your services. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact information. My department of criminal technical department, we were never given any results, any outcome, by the UN members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness, if the UN published officially their results?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you say that your services never received this official outcome, this official result, from the UN, your services since January 1994, did they contact the UNPROFOR to obtain these results? And if they have, when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, so you don't know if the service where you were a highly placed official, you don't know whether they contacted the UNPROFOR to obtain results. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about it. If they were contacted -- if they were supposed to contact anyone, then presumably the Tribunal would have had to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you yourself, you did not have any contact with the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After we finished the work, we give it to the Court, and then the Court continues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And personally speaking, you were never interested in finding out what was the result of the investigation, or where almost 110 people died?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I wasn't interested, but because of a large volume of work, we did not have time to be interested in these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Interpreter apologises, Mr. President. I said 70, not 110.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any information about what was given to the Sarajevo press at that time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a standard information that's given to the media, the newspapers, and the television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as far as you know, who was giving the information to the newspapers and to the television?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, they could have been journalists. And the police employees did not have a right to give any information to the media. The only right to have contact with the media is the Court, in fact, the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you know, did this institution give information to the media?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the Court or the police?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the institution, company institution that you mentioned; I'm talking about the Court.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know whether the Court communicated anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you, yourself, had no cooperation with the UNPROFOR immediately following the incident?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only at the time when they arrived to the site of the incident, when I showed them where the projectile was, the projectile they took out, and after they took it out and examined it, then I took it away with me. And that was the only contact with the UNPROFOR I had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you took that item with you on which date exactly?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the same date, after it was taken out by the UNPROFOR, this projectile was brought to the premises of the criminal technical department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, so we are talking about the 5th, the day of the 5th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if I understand you correctly, after the 5th, which was the day where you carried out your investigations on the scene of the incident, you did not investigate Markale any further. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the following day, I did not go to the scene of the incident where the ballistic experts who were authorised by the Court, they were the only ones who were carrying out investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said the following day, which is the 6th, the ballistic experts carried out investigations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. But on that day, on the 6th, the stabiliser was no longer in its place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following day, the 6th, since the ballistics experts went to the scenes, Zlatko Medjedovic and Hamdija Cavcic, they took the tail-fin to establish together with the expert so they could determine the angle at which the projectile landed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Witness, if I understand you correctly, the 5th, the projectile was taken out from its impact point, and it is taken away by your services? So far, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the 6th, other people returned to the site with the stabiliser that they then put in the -- back into the -- to the scene of the incident. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who worked on the 5th, the investigation, in order to determine the direction, Mirza Sabljica and Zlatko Medjedovic -- sorry, Cavcic Hamdija, the next day, they went again, the same experts of the CSB Sarajevo, they went out there and they took the projectile with them. I'm talking about the same people who were there on the first day. They were also the second day because no one else could get hold of the projectile except for these authorised people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, for what reason did these people return on the 6th to the site of the incident, since they had the whole day on the 5th to carry out their investigations?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the investigation carried on for quite a while, because of it being the month of February and days were shorter, the investigation was stopped and it continued the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But for which reason, if you know that the investigation would continue, why was this item removed from the scene of the incident, since you know that it was a vital object just in order to put it back the next day?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The projectile had to be taken out, and it was possible to simply return it the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could you give us the names of the people who were posted at night to guard the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The scene of the incident was secured by the Stari Grad police, as I said already, and it was secured for about five or six days. It was covered 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you couldn't give us the names of the people who were in charge of the security of the site?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would now like to show the witness a document which is an enlarged sketch done by experts. And if I am doing it now, it's because it would be more comprehensive rather than doing it later when we look at the second version of the tape. So we're now showing this sketch. It comes from the Defence. This is done by experts, but it would make it easier for us to understand certain things. Are we authorised to proceed? I understand there's no objection. We could, perhaps, start by showing the sketch and putting it on the ELMO. Would it be possible to tender it as evidence if this proves useful?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we start by distributing copies of what they propose to use?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you did not give, prior to the cross-examination, a copy to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not yet, Mr. President, because, Madam Registrar, I think we will tender it as exhibit. That will probably be D64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree that it should be D63, because the original D63 yesterday turned out to be the same document as a document tendered by the Prosecution. So if you would first give an opportunity to the Prosecution to have a look at it globally so... Mr. Usher, perhaps you could already give the first copy to the Prosecution so that...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see for the first time that the Prosecution is smiling. I believe that's a good sign. Mr. Stamp, is there an objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know what he proposes to do. Could counsel's comments be directed through the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I need to object, I will. I don't know what Defence proposes to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The only thing I wanted to be sure is that you would have a copy of the document in your possession against which you might have objected if you wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm just getting a copy. I have no objections to getting a copy or to the witness being shown a copy. I have no objections to what has been done so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we, Mr. Usher, put this document on the ELMO, please. There is a sufficient number of copies for everyone. Mr. President, at the same time it would be very useful if -- could the witness be allowed to handle the stabiliser which is, at the moment, to the right-hand side of Madam Registrar. Thank you very much. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have to your right a sketch, and to your left you have what you say was the stabiliser that you found in loco. First of all, I would ask you, please, if you could take the stabiliser itself and if you can have a look at its structure, sort of its code structure, its structure, precisely this. Could you please indicate, Witness, by looking at the lower part of the wings, the tails, the tail-fins -- could you please take it into your hands, Witness, please. And by looking at it this way, yes, Witness, do you see here a centrally located disk which has got certain inscriptions on the lower part of the central disk?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, around this central disk, is there a kind of ring, a fixation ring, fixing ring?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you mean this ring which is carrying the fins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, is there or is there not between the ring, the circular ring which is around the disk that you just mentioned, is there a continued seam? Now I can see you --

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. I don't know which seam you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the central disk, which has inscriptions, and the ring, which is around the disk.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. President, this corresponds, if you can see it, to the photograph number 13 perfect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, now, if we're seeing the same thing as you are, now is there a border, a seam, between these two elements, between the ring and the centrally -- the central ring? And I'm talking about a continued seam.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see a continued seam?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. President, we are going to have to modify the position of evidence on the screen. Perhaps we can look at photograph number 13, which was given -- handed over by the Prosecution, and if we can put it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is Exhibit P2262.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 13, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, you may put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we are. We can see this photograph. Perfect. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I asked you if there was a continued seam, an uninterrupted seam around the circle. Now, could you indicate what you saw which corresponds to a continued seam? Could you please take the pointer, and if you can indicate it on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, you mean this particular seam around here. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that this is this area but not the seam because personally I cannot see a seam. So could you please indicate where you yourself see a seam between these two elements?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I mean a continued seam, an uninterrupted seam.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I have to ask you a delicate question. Do you know what a seam is?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that it is broken up, this seam, if you think about this part here. It probably comes because there was some material, perhaps soil or something else nearby, because of that. What's here probably comes in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, very well. I am stopping you because I'm going to have to indicate for the transcript what you just indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, the witness circled the area of separation between the disk and the ring which is carrying the fins, and I'm talking about the seam. And then when I asked him what a seam is, the witness showed an area which is located at 4.00, if we're talking about space, roughly 4.00. We're talking on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is this what you're talking about? Now, Witness, I'm going to ask my question again. Could you show us clearly where exactly this seam is between the disk and the ring which is carrying the tail-fins on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, once again for the transcript, the witness once again circles the object, that is the whole circle where the disk is separated from the ring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what is the type of the seam? How were they soldered together?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Asking a witness who is a criminal technician trained in the collection of evidence on crime scenes about how a mortar tail-fin is souldered really invites him to give a speculated answer outside his area of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you want to put to the witness the question you just asked him would you please first ask the witness whether he has any technical knowledge on soldering and soldering techniques. And perhaps at the same time could -- but that is a different matter -- could the Court, who is the only one who couldn't see the artifact because it was behind the screen, from our point of view, could Mr. Usher give the tail-fin or the stabiliser to the Chamber. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you, during your training, receive some technical knowledge in mechanics, in mechanical subjects? Because what we're talking here about is a mechanical problem.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All that had to do with explosive devices, we were simply not trained in that at all. Our training had to do only with crime investigation. And in this case I cannot say because I do not know -- I had no hand in making this projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you for the answer. So my reasoning is -- and you will tell me if I am wrong -- you say you cannot distinguish the presence of a seam from the absence of a seam. Is that it? You don't know?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photograph, you see that it is broken. But it does not mean much. It could have been due to photography, because we were working under very hard conditions. And probably the photograph was not taken well. But I do not see that the structure of this material was destructed or damaged by some mechanical force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. President, we can look at another element, that is, change the document which is on the ELMO, and go back to the sketch which we submitted a moment ago. Perhaps in another direction. Yes, thank you. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, before we examine other technical matters, will you remind us, please, how much -- how thick was the asphalt in the market of Markale at the place of impact?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 3 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is indeed what you said yesterday. Was it concrete or what was -- was it asphalt?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was asphalt. It was an asphalt base.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is, I remember you saying that. Thank you. If you now look at the sketch that you have here, that you have to your right and which you no doubt can see on your screen, can you confirm -- but I'm trying to be very precise. This is a theoretical diagram. Can you confirm that when a shell hits the ground, then one finds more or less this type of structure in the ground?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What type of structure? I just ask for some clarification to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall be happy to clarify. "This type of structure," this means the fins in this position with this part of the body which seems to have survived after the impact, that is, the cylindrical part which we see to the right of the drawing.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is precisely in this -- it is precisely in this way how the stabiliser hits and then penetrates the ground, with the cylindrical part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when we found a stabiliser in a place, we find it there, Witness, on together with this part which we see schematically presented on the right which is presumably the residual part?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, because the body bursts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this answer. Now, I'd like you to tell me if when one takes out the stabiliser whether after it has been extracted, whether a circular crater remains in the place where the body of the shell was extracted?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely, because not much digging is done around. One digs as little as possible, and one applies tongs or things to get it by its tail and then pull it out with as little disturbance as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this answer. Did you take photographs of this lower crater? And I mean the crater, the cylindrical part of to the right of this drawing?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After the extraction, the crater was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel is speaking over the witness.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph was not taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The flaps, the fins which we can see to the left...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please stop -- no, no, no. Would you please stop before continuing when the witness is still speaking. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [[In English] I do apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'll just go back to that question: When the body falls, it lodges, or rather, it digs its own crater. But isn't it also true that the form of the upper crater, that is, the crater which is above the circular object that we just talked about, and that its shape will be slightly star-shaped because it is determined, because it is being shaped by the flaps, by the fins?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. You do not find their mark in the ground because the detonation produces the crater, and all these fins go down together -- lodge in the ground together with the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for this answer. When a projectile such as this one hits relatively hard ground such as an asphalt surface, isn't there, as a rule, a slip shift of the ring which keeps together the body with the flaps?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, not in this case. Otherwise, in all cases, the flaps were always affixed to this part of the elongated body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not talking about the fins; I'm talking about the slippage of the ring which affixes the ring. So I'm asking you the same question. Isn't it true that as a rule, the penetration force can produce the slippage of this ring which affixes the structure?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is not an objection; it's just a question of clarifying this question. I'm afraid I don't know of any evidence, or I -- perhaps I am not getting the translation exactly of what my friend said. I don't know of evidence before there being a slippage of a ring which affixes another ring. This is what the transcript reflects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand the question, whether this could happen. And then of course another question might arise, whether this is something of an opinion of an expert or something to be established by someone who has a lot of experience. So perhaps if we would first sort out what Mr. Piletta-Zanin is asking, whether this witness has a theoretical knowledge of the issue, or whether he has any practical experience with this phenomenon. Would that be --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- helpful? Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will be happy to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you investigated different incidents involving shelling. Is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, didn't you, yourself, state -- and I am quoting from memory -- that during the war you learned very quickly, and that you learned all sorts of things about calibres and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, then I am concluding that you very quickly acquired experience about -- in handling this type of weaponry?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only insofar as the things found on the site are concerned. But things that have to do with the ballistic matters, with parts of projectile and all that, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. But my question has nothing to do with ballistics. It is mechanical. It has to do with mechanics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as far as we understood the request for clarification from Mr. Stamp, would you please come to the point we just discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I shall be happy to do that. May I then continue with the fins, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the only thing -- we were talking about what was the basis of the knowledge of the witness or whether he learns it quickly or slowly or whether he learned it while wearing jeans or in sunshine or not, that's what I mean with "come to your point." The point is clear to everyone. If you would come to it, that would accelerate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then one question, Witness: You acquired, therefore, whatever the weather conditions, you acquired considerable knowledge about the material which you acquired on site, on the scene?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment ago, you mentioned -- you said that it was a question of mechanics, but I had no part in either the production or destruction of this projectiles. I do not know what damage they undergo when falling -- when impacting. What I can confirm is that no mortar shell that we found had its fins or its body separated from the fixation ring about which you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So I have the answer. Thank you. Witness, now, I'd like to go back to the question of consequences in the wake of the explosion of such a projectile. Witness, you saw several sites where such shells fell. When you arrive there, what does the crater look like? Can you see it or can you not see it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crater -- you can always see the crater, because there's a certain amount of material in it. And there are often marks of a -- how shall I call it -- of fire, so there is some soot or something depending on the ground on where it hits, whether it's asphalt or earth or concrete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when we talk about the end part of the shell, this part, would it be usually covered or visible in situ, I mean?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is always visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness. I'd like to go back briefly to another photograph which has to be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is the same as mentioned briefly, but on page 10. Can the usher please help me. It is P2262. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you just told us that the end part of the projectile, that is, what one calls stabiliser which you have before you, is always visible on site. Can you show us where do we see, where do we see the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, I did not say that you could always see the stabiliser. We were talking about the crater, and I said that the place of impact can always be seen based on the -- due to the damage that one sees, whether be it asphalt, be it concrete, be it soil. The crater is here, and the damage is all around here, and then further -- further out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I asked the question and I was checking this question on page 25, line 24, and I said, when we are -- it says: "We are talking about the end part of the shell, that is, this part." And I even said "in situ," was it visible or was it covered. And the witness said it is always visible, you can always see it. And when I asked this witness to point at the place where one could see the stabiliser in this photograph, then I note the different answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, why did you tell me a moment ago that the end part of the shell could always be seen?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you are moving from one question to another. Perhaps there was a misunderstanding. From this photo documentation and from the videorecording of Markale, one can see the crater, which is covered up, and the tail-fins cannot be seen. They cannot be seen until the arrival of UN members who came there, cleared the place, and pulled it out. And I understood your previous to mean whether one could see the place where the projectile impacted, and I said yes, that one could see the traces of the trail or even marks left by flames. But that one could always see the tail-fins in cases when the shell had lodged in the ground, then no. Sometimes you can see it; sometimes you can't. In a different set of photographs done on the 4th of February at Dobrinja, number 1 marked the place where the shell fell and where one could see the tail-fins, where it was not covered by earth in the crater. But in this particular case, the stabiliser was completely covered up in the crater and was not visible. I hope I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. On this photograph I see several things. I see a map; I see the compass; I see an arrow; and I see, also, the lower elements of what I think were part of the -- of a device used to measure space, that is the lower parts of something that was in the shape of a T.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, how could you already put markings when you still did not exactly know if the projectile was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Objection. Question, Witness, how could you already put markings...I don't think there was evidence that this witness put markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, where in the evidence until now we find that the witness has made markings?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. President, I never said -- indicated that he would be making marks. It is a interpretation problem, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say, you're asking in general how you could put --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'm asking, what I'm saying is generally speaking, how could you begin to launch your analysis if the presumed object is covered and cannot be seen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The objection this time is that counsel again asked the witness to speculate in an area of expertise which the witness does not claim to have. We will call a ballistic expert in respect to this incident. That has already been indicated. He is not a ballistic expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do not know if the gentleman wore jeans, so I note at the time this was his task. His task was investigate to -- his task was to establish where were the marks left by the shell. And if we shall have another specialist, very well. We shall take note of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the objection is denied. The witness has testified on a lot of subjects concerning these kind of measurements which he was present at various times, and he indicated to us how these measurements were done, although done by others. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that is not here. I see this is not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, will you please answer.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not marked on the basis of the stabiliser, which is wedged, lodged in the ground. It is done on the basis of marks, that is, traces found outside, outside the crater, in the asphalt or the concrete, which are due to the shrapnel. And these are used as the reference points to determine the direction from which the projectile came. And it is the next step when you embark on the treatment of the crater. And in this particular case, Sabljica and Medjedovic put the map in the place, the compass, and I cleared the ground around it so that we could see better and easier the damage in the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for this answer. Wouldn't you agree with me when I say that when generally the ground or the soil is more or less dark in this photograph, whilst the point which is at the intersection of the three sticks that we see in the upper part seems to be slightly lighter, do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, does that mean that here there is something the nature of which is different from the nature of the surrounding ground?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was pebble and sand which served as a basis, as the base layer for the asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that this is an excellent time for a break. I don't know if we are going to go by it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us an on how much time you'd still need for the cross-examination of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask -- talk with my colleague, but we have just provided the videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About half an hour, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd please be as efficient as possible. We'll adjourn until 11.00 and resume then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in a moment, we are going to view the tape, but before that, I would like to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise to my friend. Mr. President, we are having problems with scheduling having regard to the upcoming videolink section of this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was wondering if in the course of the day --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll find a moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- this Court could just set a time for the 92 bis discussions or arguments in respect to it, next week or whenever is convenient to the Court so we could schedule the witnesses who are here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me tell the parties that during the next break, I'll discuss with my colleagues when exactly we'll hear the 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Witness, we are going to continue. So in a moment, we'll see the video cassette, but in the meantime, I have some other questions for you. Were you informed of the existence of a commission or a committee that was to examine, so this is a committee or a commission that was supposed to be established, and that it was to include representatives from both parties as well as UNPROFOR representatives?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about a committee or a commission that was supposed to be established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I am now going to go on to another issue, which is -- and I quote what you said -- the "famous tunnel" that you mentioned during your last examination. Do you remember what you said?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I said that was the famous -- the miraculous tunnel, which was the only passage to get out of being surrounded, the only passage out into the outer world, to civilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. President, for the clarity of things, that was page 55, line 22 of the provisional version of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, several questions on this point. Sir, could you locate the exit or the entrance of this tunnel in the city itself, in the city of Sarajevo? And I mean Greater Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tunnel was outside of the city, in the area of the airport of the city, which was under the control mainly of the UN forces except for the entrance part, which was located outside of the front lines, outside of the firing positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us exactly the street where this tunnel exited?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It exited in Hrasnica, and the name of the street where the entrance was I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever use this tunnel yourself?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I used it on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Since I had the opportunity to see it for myself, could you confirm that this tunnel exited in the immediate vicinity of a residential house?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its exit in the area of Hrasnica was on the edge. This was the beginning of the Hrasnica area where private houses were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I mean your answer to be yes?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Now, you used it for private purposes or was it for professional purposes?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The few times I used it was strictly professional -- for professional reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Now, could you tell us where precisely the exit was of the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exit was in Hrasnica, but really the exact name I couldn't tell you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us where the entrance was?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance was in part of Dobrinja on a road which borders the airport of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us the name of the street, please.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't recall right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it next to a residential house?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the residential house comes out on to the street which is a border to the airport area, and because there is an empty space, so one part of the house was used as the passage which went underneath the road and then up to private houses, and then further on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I remember. Thank you very much. Now, to be more precise in relation to the tunnel, how was it guarded in Dobrinja? How and by whom was it guarded?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is for the interpretation, how and by whom was it guarded in Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tunnel was guarded by members of the BH army and some members of the police force that kept the outer side -- the actual tunnel was guarded by the army, and the outer and the entrance was guarded by the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you make it very specific for everyone, especially for the Chamber, which part of Dobrinja are we talking about, I, II, III, or IV?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you the exact part, whether it was I, II, III, or IV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the incident that we talked about, the 4th which preceded Markale, which happened in Dobrinja, what was the distance between the site of that -- of the location of that incident in relation to the tunnel itself, which was also located in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over 1.000 metres, over 1 kilometre is the distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, it was in the same district of Dobrinja, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the same part of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. You said the tunnel was guarded by the police force as well as by the army members. Now, you, as a policeman, could you indicate in numbers how strong were the forces who were guarding the tunnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance to the tunnel was guarded by about three to five people. The tunnel was strictly controlled, and it was not possible to use it at will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you said that you used this tunnel for strictly professional reasons. That means to conduct investigations in order to get to the areas of other incidents. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the army, Witness, did the army use the tunnel as well?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that the technical booth could now give us its assistance to start the viewing of the cassette that we would like to see that we did not get under this number by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The tape given to the booth was number -- that's 227 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That will now be played.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I believe that this has to be the cassette which begins by Dobrinja. And this does not seem to be this one, but are we at the beginning of the tape, please. Technical booth: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel. We cannot hear the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we are going to view this cassette anyway, and I would like you to go a little bit faster, to fast forward it and then I'll tell you when to stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please rewind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise. Could you please rewind. Stop. Thank you. Now, from this moment, could we play it normally, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to replay this scene for you again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask to go back, for the booth, please, just a few moments. Stop. Let's stop here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are two things that I would like to ask you about. But first of all, we're going to look at precisely what's happening now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the booth, could you play this. I would like everyone to pay attention to the facts that we have a date to the left, the left bottom corner of the screen. Could we play the tape now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here, please. Now, could you please rewind a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here. Here we are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, counsel. We cannot hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now here we have a date to the left, which is no doubt the 5th of February, 1994. And to the right we see an item. Could you please describe this item for us, please. To the right on the screen.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about the scissors, then yes, that's what they are. Yes, these are scissors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, is this not an item, these scissors that are a very specific type of scissors that are used in surgery?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that we are used in surgery, but on the market everything is being sold. On the right you can see everything. On the left, you can see also some types of keys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So even items for surgery were sold?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if there's one pair of scissors there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, for the booth -- thank you, Witness -- now slowly, could we play the tape. Is it possible to have it played slowly. If not, then at a normal pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, here we are. We can see, for the transcript, the scissors, and we still see the date of the 5th of February, 1994. Stop here, please. And here we see that the date that we had a moment ago disappeared altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, the question is the following: You told me that on the site there was only one cameraman using just one videocamera. How do you explain the fact that this date disappeared?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The explanation is that the camera was not on the entire time. There was a possibility that the cameraman using it on and off, that he simply did not switch the date on or simply erase the dates. This is a technical matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're indicating to me that there is a possibility to choose the date on the camera?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a Panasonic camera. I don't see the reason -- yes, it is possible. Yes. It's a technical matter, which programmed to work in such a way. It's nothing new.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, for the booth, could you please speed up, fast forward, the tape, and I will tell you when to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here. Thank you. Could you please go back a little. Yes, just a little bit. Go back a little bit. Here. Now, this is excellent, and I will tell you play it, and I will tell you when to stop. Thank you. Here we are. You can play it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, here we can see something which more or less corresponds to a geometrical T, which was reproduced in photographs that we saw earlier. Were the photographs taken on the same day when this video was filmed, since we do not have the date on screen?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everything was done parallelly, at the same time. The photograph and the videorecording.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I believe that we can play the tape further at a slightly increased pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here, please. Thank you. Could you please, I'm sorry, go back to the beginning. Could you please rewind to the beginning. Yes, a little bit more. Could you go forward. Stop here. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that we saw this last image, the last picture, that was for us on the screen, and we saw on the tape simply does the item that we see in someone's body, in someone's corpse, I believe that it is a limb, and this is the item we can see at the lower image, is that a shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's not shrapnel. It is a part of the tissue which is detached from the body, and it comes actually from the part of the roof of a stall in the market on which this corpse was brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are telling us -- because I'm not quite sure that you visualised my question. You are telling us that this object which seems to be a piece of metal which seems to have penetrated into something which seems to be a limb and which is towards the bottom and slightly to the right of the photograph, that this was not shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. This is tissue which comes from this part of the arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask you a different question. Witness -- Witness, bodies were taken to the hospital, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these bodies had been hit by shrapnel, that is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when these bodies were taken to the hospital, and unfortunately the bodies of those dead, I believe they still had pieces of shrapnel on them or in them?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you agree with me that one could, therefore, consider that these are very important elements of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what happened to all of those numerous pieces of shrapnel which necessarily at some point or other found themselves in the hands of the hospital personnel?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you, but we were not given those pieces. It has to do with the forensic personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you, as a policeman and a police investigator, do you know if any requests had been lodged with the hospital to acquire these pieces of -- elements of investigation?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the judge conducted the investigation, he was also the person responsible for issuing whatever order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we now have another tape. That is a videotape which we'll now give, which has the number -- at least our, V000-3822, second copy, and it says "Dobrinja and Markale." This is a document which was supplied by the Prosecution. When I say "document," I mean this exhibit, this piece of evidence, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I would like to have some clarification. On page 35.20, Mr. Piletta-Zanin said that the tape, the one that we have already seen, begins with Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: It is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my mistake, sir. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in order to avoid any confusion, the tape you want to be played now, what number has it on the exhibit list of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to ask Mrs. Pilipovic. She is better acquainted with these matters. She'll respond to me directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it is, if it is the tape which we received last Saturday, then the one that I gave you is the only number. But on the tape no other number is indicated, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You received this recently from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am told that we received it, I suppose, last Saturday, but I will check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp would you identify the -- it reads V000-3822, copy 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it pleases you, Mr. President, I don't think that this videotape has an exhibit number, Prosecution exhibit number as yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It was a tape, if you recall, I referred to last week as being something that we got last week and which you directed us to immediately disclose to the Defence, which we did. It does not have a Prosecution exhibit number as yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Until now -- it doesn't have -- it's tendered by the Defence so they can give it their number. But I want to be sure everyone knows what tape we are talking about. It then can be given to the booth and be played according to the instructions of Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. President. But since we don't have another number, we cannot give it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whatever document you want to tender, you can give it a subsequent number. And just to assist you, we were at, Madam Registrar, 64. So that would then be D64.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know when the booth will be ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we are all on the video channel, we'll see when the video starts. And would you please then guide the booth, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm waiting to get the image on the screen, but that is not the case. I'll see. I have to change the channel. Do you have the image, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not yet, so I assume they are still preparing. There seems to be a problem with the tape so that it will not play. Is this a problem that can be solved or... Mr. Stamp, do you have another copy of that same tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm making that inquiry just now, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It cannot be played. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'm quite sure you have viewed the tape before using it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, Mr. President, nothing is deliberate on the part of the Defence. We went through it last night, and very early this morning, and the tape was in perfect shape. And it was in your hands and now it doesn't work any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I saw something on the screen. And I think we have something on our screen now. I think the booth is now bringing us back to the beginning of the tape. Is that right? TECHNICAL BOOTH: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And first of all, thank you for being able to show the tape to us. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please guide the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm asking the booth, are we now at the beginning of the tape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you confirm that? TECHNICAL BOOTH: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I'd like to use now the same procedure, move rapidly -- go fast forward, and I will tell you when to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Thank you. A little bit forward, please. And a little bit more. Stop. It is now difficult. Could you now go back a little bit, please. And a little bit more. There. Stop now. It is so difficult to react. Now a little bit back, please. No, no, back. There, stop here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do we see here the impact of the shell? And if we do, will you please point at it.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area where the shell fell, I'm not quite clear really, but it is where you see this small pine tree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And still, while we are at this image, what one can imagine behind the window to the right, or as the case may be, on the left, would it be an apartment, a flat, which has evidently been -- which has apparently been put on fire?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the answer, which is not in the transcript, but which I believe was "yes."

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, this is a flat which is partially -- which has partly burnt down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move on, forward, and I'll tell you when to stop. We shall have two more stops. No, no, no, just go on. Just move forward. I said we'll have two more stops, but I will tell you when.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop, please. Stop. Just a little bit too -- now, will you go just a bit more forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask you one thing, noting that you speak perfect English, when you give instructions to the booth and they first have to be translated, if you will give the instructions to the booth in English, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [In English] What we saw a moment ago, please, will you come back to that. Stop here, thanks. Okay. Now I switch to French. May I? Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, do we see here the lower part of the shell?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see the stabiliser here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did you photograph this on site just as it was when you arrived? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, it is correct to say that this stabiliser is fully free and perfectly visible.

utterances.speaker: SEAD BESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how we found it.
