utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was here, and I was -- my back was turned to the shop, to the 22nd of December. So the building was behind me, and the shell landed to the right behind my back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm sorry, we're not talking about the shell. I have to interrupt you here. So the building --

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. We're trying to gain time, that's why this is happening. The 22nd of December building is to the right of the screen after a very long vertical line of a rectangle, and I believe that this -- I believe that these are markings of these stalls, the market stalls. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you please now use the marker to denote the building. And please use number 2. If you want -- but if you want, you can always use the pen. Just open it and close it. But now could you please mark number 2 on the building of the 22nd of December.

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, could you indicate for us what is at the number 1, but please do not mark anything. You made a cross, and you mentioned number 1. You indicated number 1. Do you know what is the name of the building that is indicated like this? No, do not write, please.

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I don't know how the building is called. This is where the supermarket was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the building that you're indicating.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the building that you're indicating on number 1, what is that building, if you do know?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: It's a supermarket. This was a supermarket, and here, this was the building of the 22nd of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Things are clear. Now, Witness, could you tell us with the pointer, as far as you know, where was the point of the impact of the shell?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: At that time, I did not know where the shell had landed. But later on, when I returned to the market --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Later.

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: -- yes, very well, later, I found out that it was -- that the shell had landed here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to put a cross there and mark it with a number "3," the location that you just indicated.

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Now, Witness, the building that you indicated with Number 2, this is the building of the 22nd of December, how many floors does it have as far as you know? If you do not recall, I can help you. If I say it has approximately six floors, do you think that this is approximately correct?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I think it's fewer than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it five or four?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: Four than that. There are business premises on the ground floor and upstairs perhaps is maybe one or two floors. Possibly one, I think one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only one floor?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Usher, if we can go back to the map, if we can see the end of the building, Mr. Usher if you would go down on the sketch on the ELMO. [In English] That's okay, thanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, madam, could you please tell us, up to -- where does the building of the 22nd of December go to, since you yourself said that there was a passage, up to how far does this 22nd of December building go?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: It's not all the building of the 22nd of December. This building is borders with the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I'm talking about the superior part of the image, the upper part, above the number 2. If we can see that the line is not finished, now, could you tell us if here, the building of the 22nd of December continues in this projection of this vertical line to the right of the image?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I think it continues a little bit further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I understood you correctly when you said it continues on? Is that what it is?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many metres approximately?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, now, let us return to the site and the issue, according to you, how many people were at the marketplace at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I don't know how many people were at the market. I know that the market was crowded. There were many people. It was a crowd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I know that you said that your sense of orientation wasn't particularly good, almost as bad as mine, so perhaps you could tell us if you can locate the north on this sketch. Would you be able to tell us where the north is on this sketch that you have to your right?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: If this is north, then this is down south, and then it is east and west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, for the transcript, the witness indicated the north being the part left -- the left part of the sketch, of the diagram that we see on the screen, which then ends by a section angle, and the south obviously being the opposite side, meaning where the building of the 22nd of December would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I didn't actually -- at the present wasn't clear to me where she indicated as north. If perhaps instead of her being put in a situation where she says north, south, east, west, if she could just point to one spot that she says is north so I know exactly where she is indicating. Firstly, may be she could be asked if she knows where it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I have a totally different question. Of course I do not know what it is that you want to establish, whether the witness is aware of the market situation or what objectively is the situation. If the last one is true, there are many means to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The question that was going to come was to find out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Was to find out from the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But of course I think the question from Mr. Stamp whether the witness would know where it is would be fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Of course, of course. [Interpretation] Yes, I'm sorry. Yes, I apologise, madam. We have a technical problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were able to tell us that such and such is north, and I believe that you are able to do that. Am I right? Could you on this map tell us one side, north, south, east, or west? If you can show us with the pointer. Please do not mark anything on the map, please. No, first of all, madam, are you able to indicate such and such a cardinal point on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I know what the cardinal points are, but I can orient myself by this picture, by this drawing. I believe east would be on this side. This would be the west then. North and south.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I first understood you meant the opposite, but could you perhaps do it once again quickly. The building of the 22nd of December is the north. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: On this sketch, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So that corresponds to the north. Is that what you're saying at the moment?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. I am not trying to put you in any delicate position. If you do know where north is, then you do know. If you don't know, it doesn't matter. Just say that. Thank you for your answer. The very last question: Witness, since you indicated for us that this building was north, do you know -- sorry, penultimate question -- do you know where the projectile came from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Again, he is asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we do not know whether it's a speculation or not. The question was whether she knows where it came from. Yes, this of course could be direction or whatever may be the answer. Yes, the question of Mr. Piletta-Zanin is whether you know where the projectile that exploded on the market came from. And there again, if you know it, please tell us. If you don't know it, then of course you can't tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I know is that the shell came behind my back. It exploded behind my back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, since you said a moment ago that you lived in Sarajevo during the war and during these events, did you hear in the local press, media, anything in relation to, number 1, a commission of experts or a team of experts that had established where this firing came from; and number 2, if you have, have you heard of a result of such commission of their investigation?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I never heard anything, nor was I really wanting to remember these events that I lived through. First of all, it was -- I was becoming very emotional about it. And it upset my family life and my life a great deal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We do not have any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp, is there any need for the Prosecution to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a couple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A few more questions to you by the counsel for the Prosecution. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect to that sketch that is in front of you, are you quite sure where east, west, north, south is or are you guessing at these directions?

utterances.speaker: EZREMA BOSKAILO
utterances.text: I'm not sure where is what. It was guesswork on my part. I know that to the right is east, to the left is west, north is up, south is down. But with this sketch before me, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Boskailo, this concludes your testimony in this Court. I think you'll now better understand why we tried to conclude it today and not let you wait for a couple of days and then return for just the last half hour. Because we are all aware that it's quite something for you. You explained to us why you came, and we do not underestimate what it means for witnesses to come from such a distance to tell this Court and to answer to the questions of the parties about those events that happened meanwhile many years ago, because it's important for this Court to hear from those who were present during these days, to hear what they have got to tell us answering the questions of both parties. Therefore, I'd like to thank you very much, since it is important for the decisions we'll have to take. So I thank you very much, and I hope you have a safe trip home. And I, of course, hope that they will be able to arrange for your return to your family as soon as possible. Thank you very much for coming. Mr. Usher --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please lead Mrs. Boskailo out of the courtroom. We'll then deal with the exhibits. We have to deal with one small technical issue, Ms. Boskailo. We'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to express my gratitude for the Defence for the format they presented the annex D66. We have two exhibits tendered. The first one is an easy one. I think that's P2265A, which is the medical report. And that may be admitted no evidence. But the second one, Mr. -- And the translation as well, that's P2265A.1. I see that we have a new number. That was my question. New number for the sketch. Madam Registrar, I better leave it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for the diagram marked by the witness is P3664.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I should have known by now that I better leave it in your hands than to take over, Madam Registrar. Thank you very much. I would like to thank all the parties and General Galic and the technical assistants and the interpreters for enabling the Chamber to excuse the witness today. Thank you very much for that. Tomorrow we'll not sit. That means that we'll adjourn until next Monday morning at 9.30. And I have to warn the parties that it might be in a different courtroom. I know that a few changes might be made either today or tomorrow. So would you please inform yourselves with the Registry whether it would be Courtroom II or another courtroom. We'll then adjourn until 9.30 next Monday in a courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
